# fjordrun_team_token (Resource)

A team API token (`fjr_...`). Creating one needs the admin role and a personal access token: tokens can't mint tokens. It acts with the role of the person who created it.

~> The API only returns the secret when the token is created, so `token` is kept in Terraform state. Use an encrypted remote state backend. An imported token has no `token` value. Tokens can't be changed: every attribute replaces the token, which revokes the old one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

# A token for one project, for a CI pipeline. Needs a personal access token: tokens can't mint tokens.
resource "fjordrun_team_token" "ci" {
  team_id    = var.team_id
  name       = "github-actions"
  project_id = fjordrun_project.shop.id
}

output "ci_token" {
  value     = fjordrun_team_token.ci.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Token name (1-100 characters).
- `team_id` (String) Team ID.

### Optional

- `project_id` (String) Limit the token to this project. Leave out for a token with access to the whole team.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time.
- `id` (String) Token ID.
- `last_used_at` (String) When the token was last used.
- `prefix` (String) The token's visible prefix.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The secret token.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# team_id/token_id. The secret itself can't be imported: `token` stays empty.
terraform import fjordrun_team_token.ci 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111/44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444
```
